question: How do independent root searches spend one fixed total simulation allowance at 1, 2 and 4 workers on three declared initial states?
scope: Computational fixed state study. No episodes or playing strength evaluation.
root_adjustment: Create the ordinary scenario from random.Random(300), then set player.pips to 7. Preserve all other state. This makes several opening actions affordable.
order: Scenario order as listed. Search seed order as listed. Worker order rotates with seed index. For each state, seed and worker count, create one fresh engine, run cold, immediately repeat with the same seed on the same pool, then close it before the next condition.
randomness: Worker seed is the unsigned integer in the first eight SHA256 bytes of ASCII mcts-root-v1:{seed}:{worker_id}, interpreted big endian. Worker ID is its allocation index. No environment progression occurs. Each search builds fresh trees even when the pool is reused.
allowance: Quotient and remainder division assigns each total across configured workers. Both ceilings apply. Complete simulations reserve the full horizon. No redistribution or retry. A 60000 transition ceiling cannot stop 12000 five round simulations early, although terminal outcomes can reduce actual transitions.
startup: Cold wall time includes engine construction, process launch and receipt of one readiness message from every initialized worker. Record that measured pool startup component separately. One worker executes locally, so it has no process startup. Warm means a second search on the same pool after the cold search, not a retained tree.
serialization: Before each measured search, serialize and deserialize its exact WorkerJob payloads using the multiprocessing ForkingPickler. Record bytes and elapsed time separately as an in-process diagnostic. This is not the actual IPC transfer time and is excluded from search wall time. Also record worker compute durations. Wall time less the longest worker duration is only composite orchestration overhead, not pure communication latency.
metrics: actual and unused simulations and transitions
wall seconds and simulations per second
payload bytes and serialization probe seconds
selected action, every root visit count and value sum
failures, unknown work and stop reasons
resource_policy: At most four worker processes on the current 8 core, 16 logical CPU machine. Pause competing agent rendering, tests and benchmarks during measurement. Preserve ordinary applications and system settings. Record observed conditions without claiming exclusive machine access. Do not expand to eight workers during this study.
analysis: Retain every cell. Compare paired worker counts within each state, seed and phase using one worker wall time divided by the other wall time. Report individual cells and descriptive medians with min and max. These seed repeats reuse one state per scenario and are not independent scenario samples. No significance tests, linear scaling claim, quality inference or result-based tuning.
failure_policy: Write the first attempt incrementally. Retain failures and partial receipts. Do not substitute serial work or rerun an unfavorable condition. Stop and retain an interrupted run. If code is corrected after a failure, use another source revision and a separate output while preserving the first attempt.
source_identity: The runner requires a clean committed tree and records its full source revision, this protocol's normalized SHA256, runtime, platform and normalized hashes for engine, game, data and the runner. Commit this protocol and implementation before the study.
reproduction: python tools/run_parallel_scaling.py --output parallel-study.json --conditions "Describe the measurement conditions"
